newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
INDO-BANGLA WATER AGREEMENT SINGNED

India and Bangladesh signed a historic 30-year accord on sharing the Ganges waters. The two countries agreed that they would receive a guaranteed quantum of 35,000 cusecs of water in alternate three 10-day periods during the worst days of the lean spell between March 1 and May 10. The treaty, signed by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina Wajed, would meet West Bengal's water requirements of nearly 40,000 cusecs, needed to flush the Hoogly river to keep the Calcutta port open.
The Hindustan Times
UPROAR IN PARLIAMENT OVER DELAY IN WOEMN'S BILL

Both the Houses of Parliament saw uproarious scenes as members cutting across party lines flayed the government's delaying tactics in introducing the proposed Women's Bill. In the lower house, the government faced flak for not categorically saying that the Amendment Bill giving 33 percent reservation to women in lower house and state assemblies would be placed in the current session of parliament. Women members across parties were on their feet even as Parliamentary Affairs Minister Srikant Jena reiterated the government's commitment to the Bill but failed provide a time framework. The upper house too saw members agitated over the government's apathy to the Bill.
Financial Express
INDIA SOFTENS STAND AT WTO MEET

India softened its stand at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) ministerial meeting at Singapore to agree to WTO undertaking a two-year study on multilateral investment and competition policy. The consent was on the condition that the study should form a prelude to the mandatory TRIMS review, which is due by 1999/2000 and not lead to any negotiations within WTO. India also softened its stand on labour standards finding place in the Ministerial Declaration.
TWO BANKS ALLOWED TO CROSS THRESHOLD INVESTMENT LIMIT IN SHARES

The central bank (RBI) allowed two public sector banks, the Bank of Baroda (BoB) and the Dena Bank, to cross the threshold five percent investment limit on shares and debentures. This selective easing up assumed significance in the context of the Finance Ministry's recent efforts to get banks to invest more in stocks. BoB has been allowed to invest an additional 650 million rupees in excess of the limit whereas Dena has been allowed to invest another 150 million rupees in this segment. Dena could invest only in non-convertible bonds, while BoB was free to invest the amount the way it liked, said sources.
CASH-STRAPPED CORPORATES SEEK DEBT-EQUITY SWAPS

Cash-starved corporates have approached banks and financial institutions (FIs) to convert a substantial portion of their equity funding proposals into debt for unfinished projects. Banks, which had extended loans for projects on the assumption that a part of the debt would be raised via equity, would have to choose between increasing their exposure in the projects without caring for the debt-equity ratio or allow the projects to die due to cash crunch. A consortium of banks and FIs are taking stock of the debt-equity-swap in the seven billion rupee Sanghi industries' cement project, in which they have a two billion rupee exposure. INVESTORS KEEN ON PUBLIC SECTOR SCRIPS

The Konkan Railway Corporation (KRC)'s two billion rupee bond issue received full subscription. Another state undertaking (PSU), Maharashtra Krishna Valley Development Corporation (KVDC), which entered the market with a three billion rupee bond issue a fortnight ago, also received good response. The KVDC issue has already garnered over three billion rupees in subscriptions. The success of the two PSU instruments showed the investor preference had shifted to PSUs. Investors were looking at safer avenues to park their funds, a banker said. Both the issues promised tax benefits for the investors under the Income tax Act. MAHARASHTRA GOVERNMENT MAY PICK UP EQUITY IN DABHOL POWER

The Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) is planning to pick up a stake in the Dabhol Power Company (DPC). The board is said to be studying the legal and financial implications arising from this exercise. MSEB is concerned about DPC being an unlimited liability company, which may pose complications in a situation of bankruptcy. According to sources, MSEB can pick up the stake in DPC through a limited company. Though MSEB was unsure if the mode of payment for the equity bought should be in dollars or rupees, sources said the payment would only be made in rupees. This would make securing permission from the central bank (RBI) easier. U.S.-based Enron would retain its 50 percent stake
25 TELECOM FIRMS FAIL TO MEET FEE DEAD LINE

Seven of the 32 cellular operators including Escotel, Bharti, Reliance, Birlacom, Tata-Bell Canada, Koshika and RPG paid up their second instalment of licence fees to the Department of Telecommunications (DoT). The deadline for its payment expired on December 12. DoT turned down the request of the companies that had not paid the second instalment of licence fees. These companies had sought a month's extension to pay up their dues.
The Economic Times
UNIT TRUST MAY DIRECT BANKS' SECONDARY MARKET FORAYS

Public sector banks may be allowed to invest in the secondary market through the Unit Trust of India (UTI). The central bank (RBI) had recently allowed banks to invest in the secondary market. But most of the banks did not venture to do so citing their lack of knowledge or experience of the secondary market as the reason. The RBI governor is learnt to have suggested that banks could entrust their funds to UTI which it would invest in the secondary market on their behalf. According to the proposal, which may be cleared after talks with UTI and the bourse regulator, the investments are likely to be made in one of UTI's equity growth funds. 55 COMPANIES SLIP INTO NON-PERFORMING ASSET CATEGORY

Fifty-five out of 60 hitherto profit-making companies funded by the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) have slipped into the non-performing asset category (NPA). This showed the tough times that the Indian industry was faced with. The 55 companies, part of a 60-company sample tracked by the ICICI, had failed to pay up their dues for two consecutive quarters, thus qualifying as NPAs. ICICI managing director K V Kamath said most of these companies were unable to pay up because of severe working capital crunches.
RAILWAYS STAY ON TRACK

Indian Railways, despite the industrial slowdown, did well in the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). During the April-September period, the Railways generated gross revenue earnings of 114.87 billion rupees, which is 48 percent of this year's budget of 245.82 billion rupees. Revenue earning freight loaded during the period was 193.42 million tonnes against a targeted 191 million tonnes. Total freight loaded was 12 percent higher in comparison to the previous year. It, however, lost 600 million rupees due to fall in higher-rated traffic. The Railways spent 27.88 billion rupees on its on going projects during the six months period.
FIFTY PCT SLASH IN SUBSIDIES BEING PLANNED

Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra has come up with a plan recommending a 50 percent reduction in all subsidies in the Ninth Plan without raising the price on that account. This can save funds for being used to return government loans and reduce the interest burden. Slashing subsidies on electricity, sugar, irrigation, food and fertilisers can reduce external and internal debt, says the paper prepared by Mishra. The minister discussed his plan during a meeting with World Bank officials. Mishra's plan provides the answers to the World Bank's refrain that India should reduce its subsidies.
Business Standard
ALTERNATE ENERGY PROJECTS ATTRACT $700 MLN FUNDS

The department of non-conventional energy sources attracted foreign aid and soft loans worth over $700 million this year to fund alternate energy projects. The largest $350 million was for the 140-megawatt solar-gas combined cycle power plant in Jodhpur, Rajasthan. The project is funded by the World Bank ($53 million). Another $200 million will come from Germany. The project will produce 35 megawatts from solar energy and 105 megawatts from a gas-based power component. The department is also in talks with German based KFW for a $300 million loan to finance various renewable energy projects, including solar lanterns, mini hydel projects and smokeless ovens. The Observer
PLAN TO TAP NRI INVESTMENT IN TELECOM SECTOR SHELVED

Proposal to treat non-repatriable investments by non-resident Indians (NRI) at par with domestic investments in the telecom sector has been shelved due to lack of consensus among the concerned departments. The move was proposed by the Department of Telecommunications to boost funds for telecom projects. The ministries of finance and industry stalled it saying the telecom joint ventures (JV) were capable enough to tackle this problem through their asset companies. The Industry Ministry opposed the move as this could let foreign partners to take control of the telecom JVs. BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX SHEDS 61 POINTS

Pivotals reacted on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) following fresh bear hammering and bull liquidation. The BSE sensitive index, which touched a high of 2,965.10 on further speculation, dropped on heavy bull unloading and closed at 2,880.26, showing a loss of 61.10 points from the previous close of 2,941.36. The BSE-100 index slumped by 23.15 points to 1,275.77.
ERICSSON CONSOLIDATES INDIAN STRATEGY

Swedish telecommunication major Ericsson has consolidated its various Indian operations into a single subsidiary, christened Ericsson Communications Pvt Ltd. Ericsson has appointed Roll Granstrom its president to maintain and expand its leading role in cellular networks and handsets. Granstrom said the Ericsson strategy in India would be to a major supplier for the emerging basic service operators and provide economies of scale to those with basic service licences in the same circle. Ericsson plans to set up a software centre at Bangalore to make the software for management systems for its AXE switches.
